findings.title: The Reorder this week table does not give the reorder answer the headline promises

location.description: the Reorder this week table in the hero (beside the text on desktop, below it on phone and tablet)

findings.viewer_experience: The owner has to compare two columns and work out the decision, and nothing sets Shelfmark next to the spreadsheet or till report they use now, so they must take the value on trust.

current.value: table has only the columns On shelf and Sold this week; no comparison with how a shop works now

findings.target: the table states the reorder decision for each title, and the page has a short comparison with how a shop works now
findings.fix_direction: Add a column that states the reorder decision for each title, and add a short comparison with how a shop works now. The maker must supply the column label, the values, and what the comparison says.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen images a table column that states the reorder decision for each title, and a short comparison with how a shop works now.

findings.title: The tablet hero paragraph and second feature note run over 75 characters per line

location.description: the hero paragraph under the headline on tablet

findings.viewer_experience: Lines slightly too long are harder to track from one line to the next.
findings.fix_direction: Set the text column to about 560 px so that both are 75 or fewer.

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of div.hero-text > p and section.facts > p:nth-of-type(2) in the tablet viewport is 75 or fewer

findings.title: On the phone the table header labels and a title wrap to two lines

location.description: the On shelf and Sold this week header cells of the table on phone

findings.viewer_experience: Wrapped headers and a wrapped title make the rows uneven and harder to scan.
findings.target: each header label and row on one line
findings.fix_direction: Narrow the Title column, or shorten the header labels, to keep each row on one line.

closed_when.check: lines of thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(2), thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(3) and tbody > tr:nth-of-type(4) > td:nth-of-type(1) in the phone viewport is 1

findings.title: On the phone the header uses three rows before the headline

location.description: the Sign in link on its own row in the phone header

findings.viewer_experience: About 150 px of the first screen goes to the header (logo, links, Sign in) before the headline.
findings.target: Sign in on the logo row
findings.fix_direction: Put Sign in on the logo row to get that space back.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees in the phone image Sign in on the same row as the logo, and the headline starting higher.

findings.title: The feature notes sit on thirds that the hero table edge does not share

location.description: the third feature note below the hero, against the table edge above

findings.viewer_experience: The hero table and the notes below it do not line up on one column line.

current.value: notes start at x 64, 461, 859 on desktop; table starts at x 737

findings.target: the third note, or the table, on one shared column line
findings.fix_direction: Align the third note, or the table, to one shared column line.

closed_when.check: left_edges in the desktop and widescreen viewports show section.facts > p:nth-of-type(3) and the table (thead > tr > th:nth-of-type(1)) on the same x

findings.title: Works with your till does not say which tills

location.description: the first feature note, Works with your till

findings.viewer_experience: The owner cannot tell whether their own till is supported.

current.value: Works with your till (no till named)

findings.target: the note names the tills it works with
findings.fix_direction: Name the tills. The maker must supply the list of supported tills.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees in all four images that the first feature note names the tills it works with.
